front: Em Dom Casmurro, o narrador não é confiável: nunca sabemos se Capitu traiu Bentinho.
pronunciation: eng DOHNG kahz-MOO-rroo, oo nah-rrah-DOHR NOWNG EH kohn-fee-AH-vehl: NOON-kah sah-BEH-mooz see kah-pee-TOO trah-EE-oo behn-CHEE-nyoo.
back: In Dom Casmurro, the narrator is unreliable: we never know whether Capitu betrayed Bentinho.
context: 'Narrador não confiável' = unreliable narrator. Capitu's supposed betrayal is Brazil's most famous literary debate.

front: Capitu tinha 'olhos de cigana oblíqua e dissimulada'.
pronunciation: kah-pee-TOO CHEE-nyah OH-lyooz jee see-GAH-nah oh-BLEE-kwah ee jee-see-moo-LAH-dah.
back: Capitu had 'the eyes of a sly, deceitful gypsy'.
context: Famous description from Dom Casmurro. 'Dissimulado' = deceitful, someone who hides their intentions.

front: O narrador de Memórias Póstumas de Brás Cubas é um defunto autor.
pronunciation: oo nah-rrah-DOHR jee meh-MOH-ryahs POHS-too-mahz jee BRAHS KOO-bahs EH oong deh-FOON-too ow-TOHR.
back: The narrator of The Posthumous Memoirs of Brás Cubas is a dead author.
context: Machado's playful inversion: not an 'autor defunto' (author who died) but a 'defunto autor' (dead man who writes). Word order changes meaning.

front: A ironia machadiana é sutil e muitas vezes passa despercebida.
pronunciation: ah ee-roh-NEE-ah mah-shah-jee-AH-nah EH soo-CHEEL ee MOOY-tahz VEH-zeez PAH-sah jehs-pehr-seh-BEE-dah.
back: Machado's irony is subtle and often goes unnoticed.
context: 'Machadiano' = in the style of Machado. 'Passar despercebido' = to go unnoticed.

front: No meio do caminho tinha uma pedra.
pronunciation: noo MAY-oo doo kah-MEE-nyoo CHEE-nyah OO-mah PEH-drah.
back: In the middle of the road there was a stone.
context: Opening of Drummond's 1928 poem. Using 'ter' for 'haver' ('tinha' = there was) scandalized critics then; today it's standard spoken Brazilian Portuguese.

front: O poema provocou escândalo por sua repetição obsessiva.
pronunciation: oo poh-EH-mah proh-voh-KOH ehs-KAHN-dah-loo pohr SOO-ah rreh-peh-chee-SOWNG ohb-seh-SEE-vah.
back: The poem caused a scandal because of its obsessive repetition.
context: 'Provocar escândalo' = to cause a scandal. Critics mocked the poem; it became one of the most famous in the language.

front: A Semana de Arte Moderna de 1922 rompeu com o academicismo.
pronunciation: ah seh-MAH-nah jee AHR-chee moh-DEHR-nah jee MEEL noh-veh-SEHN-tooz ee VEEN-chee ee DOYS rrohm-PEH-oo kohng oo ah-kah-deh-mee-SEEZ-moo.
back: The 1922 Modern Art Week broke with academicism.
context: The Semana de 22 in São Paulo launched Brazilian Modernism. 'Romper com' = to break with.

front: O Manifesto Antropófago propunha devorar a cultura estrangeira para criar algo novo.
pronunciation: oo mah-nee-FEHS-too ahn-troh-POH-fah-goo proh-POO-nyah deh-voh-RAHR ah kool-TOO-rah ehs-trahn-ZHAY-rah PAH-rah kree-AHR AHL-goo NOH-voo.
back: The Cannibalist Manifesto proposed devouring foreign culture to create something new.
context: Oswald de Andrade's 1928 manifesto ('Tupi or not tupi, that is the question'). 'Antropofagia' became a metaphor for Brazilian creativity.

front: Guimarães Rosa reinventou a língua ao misturar o falar sertanejo com neologismos.
pronunciation: gee-mah-RAYNGS RROH-zah rray-een-vehn-TOH ah LEEN-gwah ah-oo mees-too-RAHR oo fah-LAHR sehr-tah-NEH-zhoo kohng neh-oh-loh-ZHEEZ-moos.
back: Guimarães Rosa reinvented the language by mixing backlands speech with neologisms.
context: 'Sertanejo' = from the sertão (backlands). His novel 'Grande Sertão: Veredas' is famously hard even for native readers.

front: 'Viver é muito perigoso', repete Riobaldo ao longo do romance.
pronunciation: vee-VEHR EH MOOY-too peh-ree-GOH-zoo, rreh-PEH-chee rree-oh-BAHL-doo ah-oo LOHN-goo doo rroh-MAHN-see.
back: 'Living is very dangerous,' Riobaldo repeats throughout the novel.
context: Refrain from 'Grande Sertão: Veredas'. 'Ao longo de' = throughout. 'Romance' = novel (not romance).

front: Clarice Lispector explora o fluxo de consciência e as epifanias do cotidiano.
pronunciation: klah-REE-see lees-PEHK-tohr ehs-PLOH-rah oo FLOOK-soo jee kohn-see-EHN-syah ee ahz eh-pee-fah-NEE-ahz doo koh-chee-jee-AH-noo.
back: Clarice Lispector explores the stream of consciousness and the epiphanies of everyday life.
context: 'Fluxo de consciência' = stream of consciousness. 'Cotidiano' = everyday life, a key word in Brazilian criticism.

front: Macabéa, de A Hora da Estrela, é uma das personagens mais comoventes da nossa literatura.
pronunciation: mah-kah-BEH-ah, jee ah OH-rah dah ehs-TREH-lah, EH OO-mah dahs pehr-soh-NAH-zhengz MAHYS koh-moh-VEHN-cheez dah NOH-sah lee-teh-rah-TOO-rah.
back: Macabéa, from The Hour of the Star, is one of the most moving characters in our literature.
context: 'Comovente' = moving, touching. 'Personagem' is usually feminine in Brazil ('a personagem'), though both genders are accepted.

front: Vidas Secas retrata a miséria de uma família de retirantes no sertão.
pronunciation: VEE-dahs SEH-kahs rreh-TRAH-tah ah mee-ZEH-ryah jee OO-mah fah-MEE-lyah jee rreh-chee-RAHN-cheez noo sehr-TOWNG.
back: Barren Lives portrays the poverty of a family of drought refugees in the backlands.
context: Graciliano Ramos's 1938 novel. 'Retirante' = someone who flees the drought in the Northeast.

front: A cena da morte da cachorra Baleia é de partir o coração.
pronunciation: ah SEH-nah dah MOHR-chee dah kah-SHOH-rrah bah-LAY-ah EH jee pahr-CHEER oo koh-rah-SOWNG.
back: The scene of the dog Baleia's death is heartbreaking.
context: The most famous chapter of 'Vidas Secas'. 'De partir o coração' = heartbreaking.

front: Que não seja imortal, posto que é chama, mas que seja infinito enquanto dure.
pronunciation: keh NOWNG SEH-zhah ee-mohr-TAHL, POHS-too keh EH SHAH-mah, mahs keh SEH-zhah een-fee-NEE-too ehn-KWAHN-too DOO-ree.
back: May it not be immortal, since it is a flame, but may it be infinite while it lasts.
context: From Vinicius de Moraes's 'Soneto de Fidelidade'. 'Posto que' here means 'since' (literary use).

front: O soneto é composto por dois quartetos e dois tercetos.
pronunciation: oo soh-NEH-too EH kohm-POHS-too pohr DOYS kwahr-TEH-tooz ee DOYS tehr-SEH-toos.
back: A sonnet is made up of two quatrains and two tercets.
context: Poetry vocabulary: 'quarteto' (4-line stanza), 'terceto' (3-line stanza), 'estrofe' (stanza), 'verso' (line).

front: Os versos são decassílabos, com acento na sexta e na décima sílabas.
pronunciation: ooz VEHR-sooz SOWNG deh-kah-SEE-lah-boos, kohng ah-SEHN-too nah SEHS-tah ee nah DEH-see-mah SEE-lah-bahs.
back: The lines are decasyllables, stressed on the sixth and tenth syllables.
context: 'Decassílabo heroico' (stress on 6 and 10) is the classic meter of Portuguese sonnets. Syllables are counted up to the last stressed one.

front: O eu lírico expressa uma saudade que não se explica.
pronunciation: oo EH-oo LEE-ree-koo ehs-PREH-sah OO-mah sow-DAH-jee keh NOWNG see ehs-PLEE-kah.
back: The lyrical self expresses a longing that can't be explained.
context: 'Eu lírico' = the poem's speaker (not the poet). 'Saudade': longing for something absent, the most famous Portuguese word.

front: A rima é rica quando une palavras de classes gramaticais diferentes.
pronunciation: ah RREE-mah EH RREE-kah KWAHN-doo OO-nee pah-LAH-vrahz jee KLAH-seez grah-mah-chee-KAHYZ jee-feh-REHN-chees.
back: A rhyme is 'rich' when it joins words from different parts of speech.
context: Portuguese poetics distinguishes 'rima rica' (e.g. noun + verb) from 'rima pobre' (same word class).

front: A metáfora do mar como destino percorre toda a obra.
pronunciation: ah meh-TAH-foh-rah doo MAHR KOH-moo dehs-CHEE-noo pehr-KOH-rree TOH-dah ah OH-brah.
back: The metaphor of the sea as destiny runs through the entire work.
context: 'Percorrer' = to run through. 'Obra' = body of work or a single work.

front: Vou-me embora pra Pasárgada: lá sou amigo do rei.
pronunciation: VOH-mee ehm-BOH-rah prah pah-ZAHR-gah-dah: LAH SOH ah-MEE-goo doo RRAY.
back: I'm off to Pasargadae: there I'm a friend of the king.
context: Manuel Bandeira's poem of escape. 'Pasárgada' became a synonym for an imaginary paradise. 'Pra' = colloquial 'para'.

front: Morte e Vida Severina é um auto de Natal pernambucano.
pronunciation: MOHR-chee ee VEE-dah seh-veh-REE-nah EH oong OW-too jee nah-TOW pehr-nahm-boo-KAH-noo.
back: Death and Life of Severino is a Christmas play from Pernambuco.
context: João Cabral de Melo Neto's dramatic poem. 'Auto' = a medieval-style religious play.

front: O enredo é previsível, mas o desfecho surpreende.
pronunciation: oo ehn-REH-doo EH preh-vee-ZEE-vehl, mahs oo dehs-FEH-shoo soor-pree-EHN-jee.
back: The plot is predictable, but the ending is surprising.
context: 'Enredo' = plot; 'desfecho' = ending/resolution. Also useful: 'reviravolta' = plot twist.

front: A obra dialoga com a tradição regionalista de forma irônica.
pronunciation: ah OH-brah jee-ah-LOH-gah kohng ah trah-jee-SOWNG rreh-zhee-oh-nah-LEES-tah jee FOHR-mah ee-ROH-nee-kah.
back: The work engages ironically with the regionalist tradition.
context: 'Dialogar com' is a favorite verb of Brazilian critics: a work 'dialogues with' (engages with) other works or traditions.

front: O romance é narrado em primeira pessoa, o que limita a perspectiva do leitor.
pronunciation: oo rroh-MAHN-see EH nah-RRAH-doo eng pree-MAY-rah peh-SOH-ah, oo keh lee-MEE-tah ah pehrs-pehk-CHEE-vah doo lay-TOHR.
back: The novel is narrated in the first person, which limits the reader's perspective.
context: 'O que' refers back to the whole previous clause (= which).

front: Uma câmera na mão e uma ideia na cabeça.
pronunciation: OO-mah KAH-meh-rah nah MOWNG ee OO-mah ee-DAY-ah nah kah-BEH-sah.
back: A camera in the hand and an idea in the head.
context: Motto of Cinema Novo, attributed to Glauber Rocha: low-budget, politically engaged filmmaking in 1960s Brazil.

front: A fotografia do filme é deslumbrante, mas o roteiro deixa a desejar.
pronunciation: ah foh-toh-grah-FEE-ah doo FEE-oo-mee EH dehz-loom-BRAHN-chee, mahs oo rroh-TAY-roo DAY-shah ah deh-zeh-ZHAHR.
back: The film's cinematography is stunning, but the script leaves something to be desired.
context: 'Fotografia' = cinematography. 'Deixar a desejar' = to leave something to be desired.

front: A atuação da protagonista sustenta o filme inteiro.
pronunciation: ah ah-too-ah-SOWNG dah proh-tah-goh-NEES-tah soos-TEHN-tah oo FEE-oo-mee een-TAY-roo.
back: The lead actress's performance carries the whole film.
context: 'Atuação' = acting performance. 'Sustentar' = to carry, to hold up.

front: O ritmo da segunda metade é arrastado e o filme perde fôlego.
pronunciation: oo RREECH-moo dah seh-GOON-dah meh-TAH-jee EH ah-rrahs-TAH-doo ee oo FEE-oo-mee PEHR-jee FOH-leh-goo.
back: The pace of the second half drags and the film runs out of steam.
context: 'Arrastado' = dragging, slow. 'Perder fôlego' = to lose breath/steam.

front: A montagem alterna passado e presente de forma engenhosa.
pronunciation: ah mohn-TAH-zheng ahl-TEHR-nah pah-SAH-doo ee preh-ZEHN-chee jee FOHR-mah ehn-zheh-NYOH-zah.
back: The editing cleverly alternates between past and present.
context: 'Montagem' = film editing (also assembly). 'Engenhoso' = clever, ingenious.

front: A peça faz uma crítica mordaz à classe média.
pronunciation: ah PEH-sah FAHZ OO-mah KREE-chee-kah mohr-DAHZ AH KLAH-see MEH-jee-ah.
back: The play makes a scathing critique of the middle class.
context: 'Peça (de teatro)' = play. 'Mordaz' = scathing, biting.

front: O cenário minimalista obriga o público a usar a imaginação.
pronunciation: oo seh-NAH-ryoo mee-nee-mah-LEES-tah oh-BREE-gah oo POO-blee-koo ah oo-ZAHR ah ee-mah-zhee-nah-SOWNG.
back: The minimalist set forces the audience to use their imagination.
context: 'Cenário' = stage set (also scenario). 'Obrigar alguém a' + infinitive = to force someone to.

front: A crítica foi unânime em elogiar a direção.
pronunciation: ah KREE-chee-kah FOY oo-NAH-nee-mee eng eh-loh-zhee-AHR ah jee-reh-SOWNG.
back: Critics unanimously praised the direction.
context: 'A crítica' (collective) = the critics. 'Ser unânime em' + infinitive = to unanimously do something.

front: Apesar das boas intenções, o filme resvala no melodrama.
pronunciation: ah-peh-ZAHR dahz BOH-ahz een-tehn-SOYNGS, oo FEE-oo-mee rrehz-VAH-lah noo meh-loh-DRAH-mah.
back: Despite its good intentions, the film slips into melodrama.
context: 'Resvalar em' = to slip into. A useful verb for nuanced criticism.

front: Trata-se de uma obra-prima injustamente esquecida.
pronunciation: TRAH-tah-see jee OO-mah OH-brah-PREE-mah een-zhoos-tah-MEHN-chee ehs-keh-SEE-dah.
back: It's an unjustly forgotten masterpiece.
context: 'Obra-prima' = masterpiece; plural 'obras-primas'.

front: O livro é denso, mas a leitura recompensa o esforço.
pronunciation: oo LEE-vroo EH DEHN-soo, mahz ah lay-TOO-rah rreh-kohm-PEHN-sah oo ehs-FOHR-soo.
back: The book is dense, but reading it rewards the effort.
context: 'Denso' = dense, heavy going. 'Recompensar' = to reward.

front: A autora subverte o gênero romântico com um final amargo.
pronunciation: ah ow-TOH-rah soob-VEHR-chee oo ZHEH-neh-roo rroh-MAHN-chee-koo kohng oong fee-NOW ah-MAHR-goo.
back: The author subverts the romance genre with a bitter ending.
context: 'Subverter' = to subvert. 'Gênero' = genre (also gender).

front: As personagens são caricatas e carecem de profundidade psicológica.
pronunciation: ahs pehr-soh-NAH-zhengs SOWNG kah-ree-KAH-tahs ee kah-REH-seng jee proh-foon-jee-DAH-jee psee-koh-LOH-zhee-kah.
back: The characters are caricatures and lack psychological depth.
context: 'Caricato' = cartoonish, exaggerated. 'Carecer de' = to lack.

front: O título remete a um poema de Fernando Pessoa.
pronunciation: oo CHEE-too-loo rreh-MEH-chee ah oong poh-EH-mah jee fehr-NAHN-doo peh-SOH-ah.
back: The title alludes to a poem by Fernando Pessoa.
context: 'Remeter a' = to refer/allude to. Pessoa, the great Portuguese poet, is widely read in Brazil.

front: A canção de Chico Buarque usa o duplo sentido para driblar a censura.
pronunciation: ah kahn-SOWNG jee SHEE-koo boo-AHR-kee OO-zah oo DOO-ploo sehn-CHEE-doo PAH-rah dree-BLAHR ah sehn-SOO-rah.
back: Chico Buarque's song uses double meaning to get around censorship.
context: During the military dictatorship (1964–85), songs like 'Cálice' hid criticism in wordplay. 'Driblar' (to dribble) = to dodge, get around.

front: A Tropicália misturou rock, música regional e vanguarda.
pronunciation: ah troh-pee-KAH-lyah mees-too-ROH RROH-kee, MOO-zee-kah rreh-zhee-oh-NOW ee vahn-GWAHR-dah.
back: Tropicália blended rock, regional music and the avant-garde.
context: Late-1960s movement led by Caetano Veloso and Gilberto Gil, heir to Oswald's 'antropofagia'.

front: A exposição propõe uma releitura da arte indígena contemporânea.
pronunciation: ah ehs-poh-zee-SOWNG proh-POH-ee OO-mah rreh-lay-TOO-rah dah AHR-chee een-JEE-zheh-nah kohn-tehm-poh-RAH-nee-ah.
back: The exhibition proposes a reinterpretation of contemporary Indigenous art.
context: 'Releitura' = reinterpretation, a new reading. 'Exposição' = exhibition.

front: A obra de Portinari denuncia a desigualdade social.
pronunciation: ah OH-brah jee pohr-chee-NAH-ree deh-NOON-syah ah jee-zee-gwahl-DAH-jee soh-SYOW.
back: Portinari's work denounces social inequality.
context: Cândido Portinari painted 'Os Retirantes' and the UN 'War and Peace' panels. 'Denunciar' = to denounce/expose.

front: A linguagem do autor oscila entre o coloquial e o erudito.
pronunciation: ah leen-GWAH-zheng doo ow-TOHR oh-SEE-lah EHN-tree oo koh-loh-kee-OW ee oo eh-roo-JEE-too.
back: The author's language swings between colloquial and erudite.
context: 'Oscilar entre' = to swing between. 'Erudito' = learned, highbrow.

front: Lido hoje, o conto ganha novas camadas de significado.
pronunciation: LEE-doo OH-zhee, oo KOHN-too GAH-nyah NOH-vahs kah-MAH-dahz jee seeg-nee-fee-KAH-doo.
back: Read today, the short story takes on new layers of meaning.
context: Reduced participle clause ('Lido hoje' = when read today). 'Conto' = short story.

front: O livro foi adaptado para o cinema com resultado irregular.
pronunciation: oo LEE-vroo FOY ah-dahp-TAH-doo PAH-rah oo see-NEH-mah kohng rreh-zool-TAH-doo ee-rreh-goo-LAHR.
back: The book was adapted for the cinema with uneven results.
context: 'Irregular' = uneven, inconsistent (in reviews).

front: Não é à toa que o romance virou leitura obrigatória no vestibular.
pronunciation: NOWNG EH AH TOH-ah keh oo rroh-MAHN-see vee-ROH lay-TOO-rah oh-bree-gah-TOH-ryah noo vehs-chee-boo-LAHR.
back: It's no wonder the novel became required reading for the university entrance exam.
context: 'Não é à toa que' = it's no accident/wonder that. 'Vestibular' = university entrance exam.

front: A poesia concreta explora o espaço da página como elemento visual.
pronunciation: ah poh-eh-ZEE-ah kohn-KREH-tah ehs-PLOH-rah oo ehs-PAH-soo dah PAH-zhee-nah KOH-moo eh-leh-MEHN-too vee-zoo-OW.
back: Concrete poetry explores the space of the page as a visual element.
context: Brazilian 'poesia concreta' (1950s, the Campos brothers) had international influence.

front: O autor brinca com a sonoridade das palavras por meio de aliterações.
pronunciation: oo ow-TOHR BREEN-kah kohng ah soh-noh-ree-DAH-jee dahs pah-LAH-vrahs pohr MAY-oo jee ah-lee-teh-rah-SOYNGS.
back: The author plays with the sound of words through alliteration.
context: 'Por meio de' = by means of. 'Aliteração' = alliteration; 'assonância' = assonance.

front: Na minha leitura, o final aberto é uma escolha deliberada, não uma falha.
pronunciation: nah MEE-nyah lay-TOO-rah, oo fee-NOW ah-BEHR-too EH OO-mah ehs-KOH-lyah deh-lee-beh-RAH-dah, NOWNG OO-mah FAH-lyah.
back: In my reading, the open ending is a deliberate choice, not a flaw.
context: 'Na minha leitura' = in my interpretation. A good way to defend your own critical view.
